item.title: Student group demands ‘racism’ inquiry following resignation of univ. DEI chief
item.description: The Canadian Federation of Students is calling for an investigation into alleged racism linked to the resignation of Delores Mullings, Memorial University's diversity chief. They criticized the administration’s treatment of Mullings, citing microaggressions and neglect, and demanded the institution prioritize equity and anti-racism efforts. An independent inquiry is sought into these issues.

item.title: FAU professor to remain suspended for spring semester over Charlie Kirk comments
item.description: FAU professor Kate Polak, suspended for comments about Charlie Kirk's assassination, will remain on leave for the spring semester. Despite her claims of being treated unfairly, faculty Senate President Bill Trapani expressed disbelief at the extended suspension. Other professors also faced disciplinary actions for similar remarks, but none faced consequences as severe as Polak's.

item.title: Minnesota ‘ghost students’ stole $12.5 million in loans, sparking calls for new safeguards
item.description: Nearly 2,000 “ghost students” in Minnesota stole $12.5 million in taxpayer-funded grants and loans, Education Secretary Linda McMahon recently revealed in a letter to the state’s governor. The letter states that “ghost students” are financial aid applicants who “were not ID-verified and often did not live in the United States, or simply did not exist.” […]

item.title: Indiana U. professor back to class after complaint about linking MAGA to ‘white supremacy’
item.description: Jessica Adams, an Indiana University lecturer, returned to teaching after being temporarily removed for linking "Make America Great Again" to "white supremacy." Despite her reinstatement, she remains under monitoring, raising concerns about academic freedom.

item.title: National free speech group calls on Loyola New Orleans to overturn TPUSA rejection
item.description: Turning Point USA at Loyola University in New Orleans continues to face rejection.

item.title: I fled Maduro’s Venezuela. Here’s what U.S. academics get wrong about intervention.
item.description: OPINION: 'Venezuelans know authoritarianism. We lived it. We escaped it. And we will tell you that bureaucratic objections from far-off academics are not equivalent to daily repression.'

item.title: University of Oklahoma may cut 16 degrees following review by board of regents
item.description: French, Drama, and German among the degrees that could be cut.

item.title: U. Washington researcher wishes conservatives dead: ‘may there be tyler robinsons for you all’
item.description: The University of Washington is investigating researcher Mara Maughan for a comment wishing for more conservative assassinations. A spokesperson condemned violence and confirmed a review of the incident.
